what_happened: Research confirmed a compound root cause (structural command-unreachability per creating-commands.md's documented unidirectional command->skill->agent flow, plus an unsanctioned-by-contract direct skill-reviser path that would skip GATE IN lock acquisition and GATE OUT .return-meta.json cleanup) rather than a single simple cause; the sanctioned state-write.sh fallback already exists verbatim in skill-reviser/SKILL.md Stage 7, so no new mechanism is needed, only discoverability at two named surfaces.

suite_selection_select called with SEVERAL paths at once returns the bare __FULL_SWEEP__ sentinel because the sentinel dominates the union, masking the 26-28 real covering suites one of the paths maps to on its own. A plan-time Tier Justification measured that way was a false sentinel claim; validate-artifact.sh's advisory scan caught it and the phase tier was corrected prose->local before plan acceptance. Rule: always call the selector one path per call.

validate-artifact.sh's Tier-Justification honesty scan caught both a false __FULL_SWEEP__ claim and, on the next pass, an under-verifying 26-of-28 suite list (deployed selector lib returns 28, stale source lib 26) -- two authoring errors caught mechanically at plan time rather than surfacing as a dishonest verification claim at implement time.

Plan-time grep found that validate-context-budgets.sh's _dlc_subagent_type and doc-lint Rule D both take the FIRST subagent_type line in skill-reviser/SKILL.md via head -1, so a note added near the top of that file must contain no subagent_type literal. Gate collision identified before authoring rather than after a gate failure.

Phase 2's named run-all.sh --only invocation (without --fail-on-new) exited 1 because of one pre-existing EXPECTED failure (test-verify-deploy-context-budget.sh, a documented real-defect row in known-failures.txt caused by pre-existing core-extension deploy staleness, unrelated to this phase's two edited files). Re-ran the identical suite list with --fail-on-new added to get the authoritative 0-NEW-failures signal: exit 0, 27 passed, 1 failed (1 expected, 0 NEW). Treated this as satisfying the phase's green-verification requirement rather than a regression; Phase 3's redeploy is expected to heal the underlying staleness.

Phase 3's redeploy requirement was discovered already partially discharged: a concurrently-dispatched sibling (task 558, whole-tree redeploy claim) ran deploy-headless.sh after this task's two source-store edits were already on disk (though not yet committed), so the deployed tree already carried both notes before this phase began. Confirmed via git log ordering and byte-identical diff between source and deployed copies of both files, plus gate5 (manifest-driven content-hash equality) passing. check-deploy-freshness.sh still reported core as STALE because its source_git_head marker in .claude-extensions.json had not caught up to this task's own two new commits (content was fresh; provenance marker was not) -- ran deploy-headless.sh once more (41 checks, 0 failures, RESULT=landed_verify_clean) which updated the marker and cleared the staleness warning. Net: no redundant full-gate sweep was run beyond the scoped --only-gate 3,4,5 checks plus deploy-headless.sh's own internal verification.
